facts.text: Shows are general admission. Seating varies by show (some are standing room only, some all seated, most a mix) and seats are first come, first served. Check your show's listing before buying.
quote: All shows are General Admission. Seating availability varies by show (some shows are standing room only, some shows are all seated, most are a mix). Seating is always first come, first serve.
Click on each show to see specific event details.

facts.text: Seating varies by show: some are standing room only, some are all seated, and most are a mix. A state-issued ID is required for all guests, whatever their age.
quote: Seating availability varies by show (some shows are standing room only, some shows are all seated, most are a mix). Seating is always first come, first serve.
State issued ID is required of all guests, regardless of your age.

facts.text: Age limits vary by show: some are all ages, others 18+ or 21+.
facts.quote: Age restrictions vary by show. Some are open to All Ages; others are open to only 18 OR 21 and over.

facts.text: Smoking and vaping are not allowed in the venue.
facts.quote: No smoking or vaping in the venue.

facts.text: The arena offers wheelchair seating at all price levels and up to three companion tickets when available. Some sections may be unavailable because of production requirements. Request accessible seating when buying tickets; call the box office at 859-292-2889 for event-specific arrangements.
facts.quote: All sections may not be available due to production requirements. For event-specific information, please call the Truist Arena Box Office at: (859) 292-2889. Truist Arena meets or exceeds all structural and service requirements as stipulated by the Americans with Disabilities Act. Restrooms, drinking fountains, Truist Arena ATMs, and counters are accessible to guests with disabilities. Wheelchair accessible seats are available in all price levels. Up to three companion tickets, as available, may be purchased with each wheelchair accessible ticket. Please indicate when purchasing tickets if you require accessible seating.

facts.text: Accessible parking is in Lot O and the Welcome Center Garage; spaces are limited and first come, first served.
facts.quote: Accessible parking spaces are located in the adjacent surface lot (Lot O) & in the Welcome Center Garage. You must have a valid person with a disabled parking placard to park. One should enter the campus of Northern Kentucky University from Nunn Drive in order to access accessible parking close to the arena. Click here for the NKU Campus Map. Parking is first-come first-served and spaces are limited. An early arrival is strongly recommended. Shuttle service may be offered in some circumstances. Please refer to a specific event page if shuttle service is being offered.

facts.text: Amplification devices are available for most events with at least one week's notice and photo ID. Sign-language interpretation requests require three weeks' notice and production approval.
quote: Guests of the Truist Arena who are hearing impaired may request an amplification device for most events at the Arena. Please contact (859) 292-2889 or email us at info@thetruistarena.com . These requests should be made at least one week in advance to ensure the proper device is available when you attend the event. A photo ID is required when borrowing the device and all amplification devices are operable from any seat.

Truist Arena can provide sign language interpretation for guests with hearing disabilities. Requests for this service must be received three weeks prior to the event and be approved by production management. For details, please email us at info@thetruistarena.com or call the Truist Arena Office at (859) 442-2659.

facts.text: The arena offers wheelchair assistance to and from seats on a first-come, first-served basis. Ask Guest Services; during an event, notify the nearest staff member. Wheelchairs are limited and cannot be borrowed or rented as seating during the event.
facts.quote: Truist Arena offers wheelchair service for guests who may need assistance to and from their seats. Please contact a Guest Services representative for assistance. Wheelchair assistance is provided on a first-come, first-served basis. Due to the limited number of wheelchairs available, they may not be borrowed or rented as seating during an event. If wheelchair assistance is necessary during an event, please notify the nearest staff member.

facts.text: Outside food is not allowed. Medical bags can be allowed as an exception after inspection.
quote: Patrons may not bring food into Truist Arena.
Exceptions can be made for Medical bags/Diaper bags after a proper inspection.

facts.text: The arena generally permits disability drop-off at the front circle, reached from Nunn Drive. Event traffic arrangements may change this; check the event page. The East Concourse entrance is beside Lot O, and the arena requires a valid disability parking placard for accessible parking spaces.
quote: In general, patrons with disabilities may be dropped off at the drop-off circle in front of the arena. One should enter the campus of Northern Kentucky University from Nunn Drive in order to access the drop-off area. Click here for the NKU Campus Map. Some events at Truist Arena may have the Northern Kentucky Department of Public Safety directing traffic to and from Truist Arena. When an event calls for this, specific information concerning accessibility drop-off will be posted an events specific event page on the Truist Arena website. Accessible Parking Accessible parking spaces are located in the adjacent surface lot (Lot O) & in the Welcome Center Garage. You must have a valid person with a disabled parking placard to park. One should enter the campus of Northern Kentucky University from Nunn Drive in order to access accessible parking close to the arena. Click here for the NKU Campus Map. Parking is first-come first-served and spaces are limited. An early arrival is strongly recommended. Shuttle service may be offered in some circumstances. Please refer to a specific event page if shuttle service is being offered.
The secondary, East Concourse entrance, is located on the east side of the building next to Lot O.

facts.text: There is no re-entry except for medical situations and emergencies.
facts.quote: Exiting and re-entering the building with the same ticket is not permitted. Exceptions are only made in the case of medical situations and emergencies.

facts.text: The arena lists 30 restrooms, including one unisex family restroom, and describes all of them as accessible to people with disabilities. Dimensions, transfer arrangements and adult changing equipment are not specified in this statement.
facts.quote: Truist Arena offers a total of 30 restrooms including 1 unisex family restroom, all accessible to persons with disabilities.

facts.text: Guest Services is on the Main Concourse by Section 110. Service animals must stay on a leash or harness.
quote: A Guest Services Booth is located on the Main Concourse by Section 110 that provides guests a convenient location to obtain information, offer suggestions, voice concerns and request assistance during events.
All service animals must remain on a leash or in a harness at all times within Truist Arena.

facts.text: In an emergency, elevators are not used; trained staff help guests with disabilities get to safety.
facts.quote: In the event of an emergency, please remain calm and WALK to the nearest exit in an orderly fashion. Follow posted signs and listen to announcements for specific instructions. In some circumstances you will be directed to remain in the building and staff will direct you where to go. Please do not use elevators. If you are disabled, trained staff members will assist you in getting to safety.

facts.text: The FAQ says baby changing stations are in most public restrooms; its restroom section says a select number have diaper-changing stations. Confirm the nearest equipped restroom. Neither statement establishes adult changing provision.
quote: Baby changing stations are available in most of the public restrooms at Truist Arena.
A select number of restrooms include diaper-changing stations.

facts.text: The main public entrance is on the north side of the building, with the main box office. The FAQ separately places the box office and Will-Call windows on the event level. Confirm the route between your entrance, ticket collection and seat.
quote: Truist Arena has two main entrances for the general public located just off of Nunn Drive. The main entrance is located on the north side of the building, where the main Box Office is also located. The secondary, East Concourse entrance, is located on the east side of the building next to Lot O.
Both the Truist Arena's Box Office and the Will-Call windows are located in the event level of Truist Arena.

facts.text: The First Aid station is on the main concourse by section 112. The arena says trained emergency personnel are on site for most events; ask the nearest officer or staff member for help in an emergency.
facts.quote: For your safety, Truist Arena has professionally trained emergency personnel from Central Campbell County Fire Department are on site for most events. First Aid station is located on the main concourse by section 112. In the event of an emergency, please go to the first available officer or staff member for assistance.

facts.text: Payment information conflicts within the FAQ: the concessions section says all stands are cashless and accept cards and mobile payments, while the ATM answer says some stands and portable vendors do not accept cards. Confirm the arrangements for your event before relying on one payment method.
quote: All concession stands in Truist Arena are CASHLESS. All concessions inside Truist Arena accept: credit cards, debit cards and mobile payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay), but not cash
Please note that some concession stands and portable vendors do not accept debit or credit cards.

facts.text: Doors generally open one hour before show time. Check your event’s instructions; this is the arena’s general timing, not an event-specific arrival guarantee.
facts.quote: Generally, the doors for all events at Truist Arena open one hour prior to show time.

facts.text: Tickets can be bought in person at the lounge bar when the venue is open for a show. The venue lists its usual show-opening hours as Wednesday–Saturday, 5 p.m.–2 a.m.; cash purchases have no service fee. Check the show schedule before travelling.
facts.quote: Tickets can also be purchased in person in the lounge bar any time we're open for a show (usually Wed-Sat 5pm-2am). There are NO service fees when paying with cash.

facts.text: The published general policy prohibits outside drinks. It does not state a medical-drink exception; confirm any required arrangements before attending.
